slides.title: What really makes a bearing fast?
slides.sub: It is not the number printed on the shield

slides.title: The races decide the roll
slides.body: The inner and outer races are the surfaces the balls run on. Rounder, smoother races with tighter tolerances lose less energy on every rotation.

slides.title: Steel or ceramic balls
slides.body: Steel balls are tough and forgiving. Ceramic balls are harder, lighter and rounder, so they run cooler and hold their speed for longer.

slides.title: Inside a 608 skate bearing
slides.caption: The races, balls and cage of a standard 608 bearing, 8 by 22 by 7 mm.

slides.title: ABEC measures tolerance, not speed
slides.body: A well made ABEC 7 will beat a badly made ABEC 9 every time. Treat the number as one clue, not as a score.

slides.title: Check 608 or 627 before you buy
slides.body: Most inline speed skates use 608 bearings with an 8 mm bore. 627 has a 7 mm bore. They look alike in a photo and will not fit each other.

slides.title: New set feels slow? Check the spacer
slides.body: Without the right spacer, the axle squeezes the inner races together and the roll dies. Tighten until the wheel spins freely with no side play.
